title: Geometric fibre of a morphism over a point
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $y\in Y$ be a point with residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $\overline{\kappa(y)}$ be a chosen algebraic closure of $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$ be the composite of the morphism induced by $\kappa(y)\to\overline{\kappa(y)}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with the canonical morphism; it is a geometric point of $Y$ lying over $y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. The *geometric fibre* of $f$ over $y$ is the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]

$$
 X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}
$$

along $\bar y$, a scheme over $\overline{\kappa(y)}$ through the second projection; equivalently, it is the base change [def-pc-base-change] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] along $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$. Up to isomorphism over $\overline{\kappa(y)}$ it does not depend on the choice of algebraic closure.
